## C2 — Test-requirement confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A07
The acuity rule of 20/40 is measured in each eye on its own, while the 140-degree rule is about how wide your continuous field of vision is, so they are two separate vision standards. [A07]
Why it matters: group_hint vision-standards; prereq_hint sec01-F04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec01-F06, sec01-F07.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A07
License qualification requires binocular vision alongside twenty-over-forty acuity per eye and a continuous one-hundred-forty-degree field of view [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint vision-standards; prereq_hint sec01-F04; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec01-F05, sec01-F06.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A07
The vision screening may be done by the MVA or by your own eye doctor, whereas the knowledge test is taken only at an MVA location. [A07]
Why it matters: group_hint test-logistics; prereq_hint sec01-F02; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec01-F04, sec01-F11.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A07
The knowledge test covers laws, safe driving practices and signs, while the skills test checks actual driving on public roads and on a course at the test site. [A07]
Why it matters: group_hint licensing-tests; prereq_hint sec01-F02; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec01-F10, sec01-F14.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A07
Needing corrective lenses does not disqualify you; it means you must always wear them behind the wheel and your license states that condition. [A07]
Why it matters: group_hint vision-standards; prereq_hint sec01-F06; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec01-F08.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A08
The supervising driver must come with you to the test site, but during the drive itself only you, the examiner and, if needed, an MVA-approved interpreter may be in the car. [A08]
Why it matters: group_hint skills-test-day; prereq_hint sec01-F20; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec01-F20, sec01-F21.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A08
Current plates and registration and proof of insurance are paperwork conditions on the test vehicle, while being safe, having a clear windshield and at least a half tank of gas are physical conditions. [A08]
Why it matters: group_hint test-vehicle; prereq_hint sec01-F16; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec01-F16, sec01-F17, sec01-F18, sec01-F19.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A08
Reporting a medical condition that could affect your driving is a legal duty you start yourself, unlike the extra requirements the MVA tells you about. [A08]
Why it matters: group_hint medical-reporting; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec01-F23, sec01-F03.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]
